entry_point.code: static const char *match (MatchState *ms, const char *s, const char *p) {

trace.code: luaL_error(ms->L, "pattern too complex");  /* MAXCCALLS=200 depth limit added by 124bc7e */
match(ms, s + 1, p + 2)  /* one C frame per input character for each .? item; unbounded before the fix */
static int str_find_aux (lua_State *L, int find)  /* string.find/string.match entry point */

preconditions: attacker can run a Lua script on the server (EVAL/EVALSHA/FUNCTION) or an application passes attacker-controlled patterns to Lua string.find/string.match
pattern and subject are large (~1 MiB each) so the recursive match() exhausts the 8 MiB C stack

evidence.vulnerable_version: redis unstable before 124bc7e (parent 63cf48ce); every stable release checked (8.10.3, 8.4.4, 8.0.6, 7.4.12) still ships the unbounded match()
evidence.fixed_version: 124bc7e (2026-11-09, unstable); shipped in 8.12-rc3 (2026-11-12); not in any stable release at disclosure
evidence.observed_result: Real redis-server built from source at 63cf48ce dies with SIGSEGV when a client sends EVAL "return string.find(string.rep('a', 2^20), string.rep('.?', 2^20))" 0. The EVAL is sent as ACL user "luauser" (+eval +ping only): its SHUTDOWN NOSAVE is refused with -NOPERM, yet its EVAL still kills the process. The build at 124bc7e replies '-ERR user_script:1: pattern too complex' and stays alive (PING -> +PONG).

real_exploit.target: redis/redis bundled Lua 5.1 deps/lua/src/lstrlib.c match() recursion, reached through EVAL
real_exploit.backend: two real redis-server binaries built from upstream source at commit 63cf48ce (vulnerable parent) and 124bc7e (fixed); the driver starts each server, creates the restricted ACL user, authenticates as it, proves SHUTDOWN is -NOPERM, sends the crafted EVAL over a real RESP/TCP connection, and checks the process exit status
real_exploit.demonstrated: an ACL-restricted user holding only scripting rights (+eval +ping, SHUTDOWN denied with -NOPERM) crashes the server with SIGSEGV by exhausting the C stack in Lua match(), while the fixed server returns the Lua 'pattern too complex' error and continues serving - a remote denial of service that crosses a real privilege boundary

evidence.notes: Fixed by porting Lua upstream's MAXCCALLS=200 match-depth limit; the fix is on unstable and in 8.12-rc3, absent from stable 8.10.3/8.4.4/8.0.6/7.4.12. Requirement: a client with EVAL/EVALSHA/FUNCTION rights (a default no-auth server makes that every client, PR:N); the PoC demonstrates the narrower ACL-confined case, hence 6.5 / PR:L. Impact is availability only (process crash).
